correctness.rationale: For a complex vector \(z\), a phase rotation diagonalizes the real/imaginary Gram matrix, reducing \(|\operatorname{Re}(e^{-i\theta}z)|^2\) to \(\lambda\cos^2\theta+(1-\lambda)\sin^2\theta\) with \(\lambda\in[1/2,1]\). For \(0<c\le1/\sqrt2\), the angular set where the real projection exceeds \(c|z|\) has measure at least \(4\arccos c\), with the collinear case extremal. Averaging this indicator estimate and applying Mukherjee’s real-input weak constant \(2\) to \(\operatorname{Re}(e^{-i\theta}f)\), together with \(\int_0^{2\pi}|\operatorname{Re}(e^{-i\theta}w)|d\theta=4|w|\), gives \(2/(c\arccos c)\). Maximizing \(c\arccos c\) yields \(c=\cos\theta_*\) with \(\theta_*\tan\theta_*=1\). Fresh numerical solution gives \(c_*=0.65218462390919\) and \(C_\mathbb C=3.5644502804062665\), matching the claim.

The phase-measure lemma is reusable for Hilbert-valued complexifications and the optimization identifies the exact constant of this method. final_claim: Let \(L_v=-\Delta-2v\cdot\nabla\) on \(L^2(\mathbb R^n,e^{2v\cdot x}dx)\), \(v\ne0\), and let \(\mathcal R_v^\mathbb C\) be the componentwise complexification of the full vector Riesz transform. Then every complex \(L^1\) input satisfies the dimension- and drift-free weak endpoint bound \(\|\mathcal R_v^\mathbb C f\|_{L^{1,\infty}(\mu_v;\mathbb C^n)}\le C_\mathbb C\|f\|_1\), where \(C_\mathbb C=2/(c_*\arccos c_*)=3.564450280406266\ldots\), \(c_*=\cos\theta_*\), and \(\theta_*\tan\theta_*=1\). No optimality of \(C_\mathbb C\) is claimed.
scientific_limitations: No claim is made that \(3.564450280406266\ldots\) is the optimal complex weak-type constant.
The proof depends on the real-valued constant-2 theorem as an input.
